title: Private Deployments — VPC & On‑Prem: Consolidated Deployment + Day‑2 Ops Guide
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose

This consolidated guide describes recommended reference architectures, customer requirements, packaging options, deployment checklists, and day‑2 operational procedures for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on‑prem / air‑gapped). It is intended for Solutions Engineers, SREs, and Customer Ops teams executing or supporting Private deployment projects.

Scope

- VPC (customer VPC with Transit/GW peering or PrivateLink) deployments
- On‑prem / air‑gapped (installer image + offline artifact delivery) deployments
- Day‑2 operations: monitoring, backups, scaling, upgrades, and rollback
- Reference deployment checklists and ownership map

Summary of recommended SLOs and operational targets

- Control plane availability (customer-facing console and API): 99.95% monthly
- Inference endpoints (per-customer dedicated pool): 99.9% monthly (for Dedicated mode within Private)
- P50 token latency (local LAN): < 30ms; P99 streaming token latency: < 250ms (model dependent)
- Model artifact sync success: 100% for each scheduled rollout; retry budget: 3 attempts
- Backup RPO (critical configs + DB): 1 hour; RTO target: 2 hours for failing-over control plane components

1) Reference architectures (high level)

A. VPC deployment (recommended for cloud-hosted private deployments)

- Topology options: private control plane (managed by Redwood) + customer-hosted data path vs fully private control plane (customer-managed)
- Core components inside customer VPC: router / gateway (NGINX), inference pool (Kubernetes node pools with GPU instances), storage (S3-compatible object store or cloud bucket), database (Postgres/Aurora), Kafka or Kinesis for async work queues (optional), Prometheus + Grafana, Loki/Fluentd for logs
- Network: restrict inference nodes to private subnets; egress through NAT or Egress Gateway; optional PrivateLink or Transit Gateway for connectivity to Redwood control plane

Recommended sizing (starting point per 1000 QPS-equivalent inference units):

| Component | Example instance / cluster size | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| GPU node pool | 4 x p4d.24xlarge (or equivalent) | supports 16 concurrent high-throughput streams |
| Control plane | 3 x m5.large (or equivalent) | highly available K8s control nodes for control services |
| Metadata DB | db.r6g.large | multi-AZ recommended |
| Object storage | 500 GB | model artifacts + snapshots |

B. On‑prem / Air‑gapped deployment (recommended for regulated customers)

- Delivery model: installer image (OCI tarball) + artifact bundle (model weights & runtime images) delivered via secure physical transfer or private object host.
- Packaging: Kubernetes manifests + Helm chart + operator for local lifecycle management. Optionally a VM packaged installer for virtualization-first customers.
- Required infra: local registry (Harbor/Artifactory), NFS or clustered storage (Ceph), on‑prem PG cluster or CockroachDB for multi-datacenter, internal load balancing (HAProxy/NGINX), GPU-enabled hosts with driver compatibility matrix documented below.

2) Customer requirements library (pre-deployment checklist)

Provide this checklist to customers early in the onboarding process. Items marked REQUIRED must be satisfied before scheduling production cutover.

- Account & billing: signed PO or contract (REQUIRED)
- Networking:
  - VPC CIDR ranges and subnets for control plane + inference nodes (REQUIRED)
  - BGP / Transit / PrivateLink details (if connecting to Redwood control plane) (REQUIRED for managed-control-plane option)
  - Firewall rules permitting internal gRPC/HTTP between nodes and ports 22, 6443, 2379 (etcd), 9090 (Prom), 9200 (optional), and custom ranges for model RPCs
- Identity & access:
  - KMS/HSM integration spec (if customer requires key ownership)
  - Service accounts and least-privilege IAM roles for S3 access, DB access, and logging (RECOMMENDED)
- Compute & storage:
  - GPU type (NVIDIA driver version), node count, and OS image (REQUIRED for on‑prem)
  - Object storage endpoint, credentials, and bucket layout (REQUIRED)
  - Backup retention policy and snapshot location (REQUIRED)
- Security & compliance:
  - SOC2 / ISO mapping (Redwood can provide evidence)
  - List of compliance constraints (data residency, retention, logging controls)
- Operational contact list and escalation matrix (names, emails, PagerDuty) (REQUIRED)

3) Packaging and installation (VPC and on‑prem)

A. Packaging components delivered to customers

- Installer bundle: tarball containing Helm charts, CRDs, operators, and deployment scripts (.tar.gz)
- OCI images: runtime images, sidecars, and model runner images pushed to customer registry or provided as tarballs
- Artifact bundle: model weights, quantized artifacts, and cached layers
- Deployment manifest: environment-specific values.yaml and example kustomize overlays

B. Example installation (helm + registry) — cloud/VPC (reference)

1. Create namespace and secrets:

kubectl create namespace redwood-private
kubectl create secret generic s3-credentials --from-literal=access_key=REDACTED --from-literal=secret_key=REDACTED -n redwood-private

2. Add Helm repository and install:

helm repo add redwood https://helm.releases.redwood.ai/charts
helm repo update
helm install redwood-controlplane redwood/controlplane -n redwood-private -f values-vpc.yaml

3. Validate pods and services:

kubectl -n redwood-private get pods
kubectl -n redwood-private get svc

C. Example installation — air-gapped / on‑prem (reference)

1. Load images into local registry (Harbor):

skopeo copy --src-tls-verify=false --dest-tls-verify=false docker://registry.redwood.ai/runtime:1.5.0 docker://harbor.local/redwood/runtime:1.5.0

2. Apply CRDs and install operator with local image override in values-onprem.yaml

kubectl apply -f crds/
helm install redwood-operator ./charts/operator -n redwood-private -f values-onprem.yaml

3. Inject model artifacts into object store and seed the operator model registry

aws s3 cp model-bundle.tar s3://local-bucket/models/ --endpoint-url=https://minio.local

4) Day‑2 operations and runbooks

A. Monitoring and observability (owner: eng-sre / customer SRE)

- Prometheus metrics to collect: inference_queue_depth, token_latency_p50, token_latency_p95, active_streams, kv_cache_hit_rate
- Alerts (examples):
  - P99 token latency > 500ms for 5m -> P1 alert to oncall
  - Control-plane API 5xx rate > 1% for 10m -> P2 alert
  - Model sync failure > 3 attempts -> P2 alert
- Dashboards: per-customer model dashboard, per-node GPU utilization, per-route latency, rollout health

B. Backups and snapshots (owner: eng-platform / customer ops)

- Postgres snapshot: daily logical backups + WAL shipping retained for 7 days
- Object storage: immutable snapshots of model artifacts before any rollout; retain 30 days by default
- Restore test: quarterly DR drill to validate DB and object store restores

C. Scaling guidance (owner: eng-sre)

- Horizontal: add GPU nodes to node pool; kube autoscaler policies recommended: 30% CPU buffer and GPU eviction threshold 85%
- Vertical: use larger GPU instances for inference-heavy models (see quantization guidance in quantization-profiles)
- Batching: enable adaptive batching with thresholds tuned to workload—start with 20ms batching window and 32 token batch size for chat endpoints

5) Upgrade and rollback procedures (owner: eng-platform / eng-serving-runtime)

Principles:
- Prefer canary + progressive rollout for control plane and model runner changes
- Always snapshot DB and object storage before schema or artifact upgrades
- Keep an index of compatible runtime-image + model-weight versions (compat matrix)

A. Control plane upgrade (minor patch example)

1. Preconditions:
  - Verify CI artifacts signed and checksums match
  - Run preflight checks (kubectl cluster-info, storage write/read test)
  - Ensure backups completed within last 60 minutes
2. Canary rollout:
  - Deploy new control-plane replica in canary namespace or tainted node pool
  - Run smoke tests: auth flow, health-check endpoints, API create/list operations (automated test suite)
  - Monitor: 10 minutes for errors, latency impact, and resource pressure
3. Progressive rollout:
  - Uncordon nodes and roll control plane with maxUnavailable=1 and maxSurge=1
  - Wait for each upgrade step to pass smoke tests and for Prometheus alerts to be green
4. Post-upgrade validation:
  - Run end-to-end inference tests against a golden prompt set (expected tokens / latency threshold)
  - Verify model sync and artifact checksums

Rollback (if canary fails):
  - Revert Helm release to previous chart image: helm rollback <release> <revision>
  - If DB schema change caused failure, run restore from snapshot and open incident bridge

B. Model runner / runtime upgrade (major changes)

1. Preconditions: ensure compatibility table lists the new runtime version and models tested
2. Canary per-customer model: deploy runtime change to 5% of traffic (route-level traffic split)
3. Validate inference quality with automated eval harness (check for regressions vs baseline prompts)
4. If quality or latency regressions detected -> rollback via traffic split revert and redeploy previous runtime image

6) Rollback checklist (fast reference)

- Stop new release traffic (update ingress / router)
- Helm rollback control-plane release
- Restore DB snapshot (if required)
- Re-seed model artifacts from last known-good snapshot
- Communicate to stakeholders and update incident bridge notes

7) Validation tests and automation (owner: eng-developer-experience)

- Smoke tests (automated): health endpoints, auth, ability to start a session, token stream sanity
- Golden eval set: 50 canonical prompts per customer to validate generation fidelity within defined thresholds (WER/acceptance metrics documented in eval-harness)
- Load test: run k6 or locust load tests at 1.5x expected peak for 30m before cutover

8) Escalation and ownership map

- First responder (P1 inference outage): customer oncall -> Redwood SRE oncall (pager) -> Eng-serving-runtime lead (pager escalation)
- Upgrade playbook owner: eng-platform (primary) with eng-serving-runtime (secondary)
- Compliance questions: security-and-compliance team

9) Templates and example commands

- Helm rollback example:
helm rollback redwood-controlplane 2 -n redwood-private

- Model sync validation checksum (example):
sha256sum model.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}' # compare with recorded checksum

- DB logical backup example (pg_dump):
PGPASSWORD=$DB_PASS pg_dump -h $DB_HOST -U readonly redwood_metadata > metadata_backup.sql

10) Appendix: driver & runtime compatibility (summary)

- NVIDIA driver (host) -> CUDA -> cuDNN -> container runtime mapping table (customer-specific file supplied in installer bundle).
- Known incompatibilities: older Ubuntu 18.04 kernels with NVIDIA 495 drivers may fail device plugin initialization—require kernel >= 5.4.

References and related pages

- Deployment playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-playbook-2026
- Reference architectures & day2 ops: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-reference-architectures-and-day2-ops-2026
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles

Contact and support

For deployment scheduling and preflight checks, contact the Private Deployments PM: private-deployments@redwood.ai. For oncall escalation use the Redwood PagerDuty integration (internal).

Document maintenance

Owner: eng-platform. This document is reviewed quarterly and after every major private-deployment project.
